title: Hiring Staff & Work Permits in Türkiye: 5-Turkish-Employee Rule
metaDescription: Learn Türkiye's 2026 work permit rules: 5-Turkish-staff ratio, exemptions, ÇSGB timelines, SGK employer costs, and tourist Ikamet work bans.
quickAnswer: Under Türkiye's 2026 [Ministry of Labour and Social Security (ÇSGB)](https://www.csgb.gov.tr/uigm/en/calisma-izni/calisma-izni-turleri/) evaluation criteria, a Turkish company sponsoring a foreign employee must generally employ at least five full-time Turkish citizens per foreigner and meet paid-in capital (500,000 TRY) or turnover thresholds. Exemptions exist for qualifying tech, R&D, and high-turnover firms, and working on a tourist İkamet is strictly illegal.

body.text: Expanding a team in Türkiye means planning local hiring and foreign work permits together from day one. Many foreign founders assume they can incorporate a Turkish company and immediately relocate senior international managers on short-term residence permits—only to discover strict labor-quota rules after signing an office lease. At [Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/), our two founders coordinate business-scouting trips, executive visits, and independent introductions on a transparent, client-paid flat fee ("Paid by our clients. Independent of provider commissions."). Formal immigration filings, employment contracts, payroll registration, and tax advice belong strictly to licensed Turkish attorneys, certified public accountants (SMMM), and official authorities.
What is the 5-Turkish-citizens-per-foreigner work permit ratio and when are exemptions granted?

Under International Labour Force Law No. 6735 and [2026 ÇSGB evaluation criteria](https://www.garsconsulting.com/blog/turkey-work-permit-criteria-foreigners-csgb-guide-2026), an employing workplace must have at least five Turkish citizens registered on SGK payroll for every single foreign national applying for a work permit, alongside at least 500,000 TRY in paid-in capital (or 8 million TRY in annual gross sales).

For a foreign shareholder-director who owns at least 20% of the company (meeting the minimum capital-share threshold), the five-Turkish-employee requirement is typically waived during the first six months of the initial one-year permit, though it must be satisfied during the second six months to qualify for renewal. Beyond shareholder grace periods, the [Ministry of Labour (UİGM) Exemptions Framework](https://www.csgb.gov.tr/uigm/en/exemptions/muafiyet-turleri/) and 2026 sectoral updates provide targeted exemptions or relaxed quotas for:

items: Information technology & software firms: Qualifying tech and R&D companies can receive quota exemptions for their first two specialized foreign hires.
High-turnover & export enterprises: Companies exceeding elevated annual net sales or export thresholds defined by ÇSGB may qualify for streamlined review.
Foreigners married to Turkish citizens or long-term residents: Individuals holding specific family or long-term legal ties in Türkiye may be evaluated under separate statutory exemptions.

Short-term statutory exemptions: Specific temporary assignments (such as machinery installation, maintenance, or board attendance) may qualify for a formal Work Permit Exemption applied for via the [ÇSGB e-İzin portal](https://calismaizni.csgb.gov.tr/en/general-information/payment-of-fees-and-valuable-paper-fees/).

body.text: How long does a Ministry of Labour work permit application take?

Once the employer submits a complete electronic application through the [ÇSGB](https://www.csgb.gov.tr/uigm/en/calisma-izni/calisma-izni-turleri/) portal—and, for consular applications, the applicant completes their Turkish embassy appointment abroad—official evaluation typically takes 30 to 45 calendar days. Incomplete filings, missing diploma translations, or quota verification questions can extend processing to 60 days or more.

Applicants who already hold a valid Turkish residence permit with at least six months remaining (excluding short-term tourist permits that are restricted for domestic conversion where applicable) can often apply domestically, as noted by the [Presidency of Migration Management (Göç İdaresi)](https://en.goc.gov.tr/work-permit). Otherwise, the applicant initiates the process at a Turkish consulate in their country of citizenship or legal residence using a 16-digit reference number, which the Turkish employer then links in the ÇSGB portal within 10 business days.
What social security (SGK) and payroll costs apply to employers?

In 2026, Türkiye's statutory gross minimum wage is 33,030 TRY per month (28,075 TRY net), and employers pay standard Social Security Institution (SGK) and unemployment insurance contributions of 23.75% on top of gross salary (reduced to 18.75% for qualifying manufacturing employers under the 5-point incentive), according to [2026 Turkish employer payroll benchmarks](https://www.teamed.global/country-hiring-guides/turkey/cost-breakdown).

Foreign work-permit holders are also subject to minimum salary multipliers based on role (ranging from 1.5x to 5x the gross minimum wage depending on whether the role is technical specialist, engineer, or senior executive).

Work permit fees and valuable paper charges are updated annually on January 1 under the [ÇSGB Fee Schedule](https://calismaizni.csgb.gov.tr/en/general-information/payment-of-fees-and-valuable-paper-fees/). Always ask a licensed Turkish SMMM accountant to run a role-specific gross-to-net cost sheet before issuing offer letters.
Why can you NOT work on a tourist Ikamet?

A short-term tourist residence permit (Turistik İkamet) issued by [Göç İdaresi](https://en.goc.gov.tr/residence-permit-types) grants only the right to stay in Türkiye—it carries zero legal authorization to work for a Turkish company or perform local commercial duties. Working without a valid ÇSGB work permit exposes both the individual and the employer to steep administrative fines, permit cancellation, deportation, and multi-year entry bans.

By contrast, an approved Turkish work permit automatically functions as a valid residence permit for its duration, enrolls the employee into Türkiye's state healthcare system (SGK), and counts toward long-term residency eligibility. faq.q: Does a Turkish work permit replace a residence permit (İkamet)?
faq.a: Yes. Under Law No. 6735, an approved Turkish work permit legally serves as a residence permit for the same validity period, so the employee does not need a separate İkamet card.

faq.q: Can a foreign company director attend board meetings in Türkiye without a work permit?
faq.a: Non-resident foreign shareholders and board members visiting briefly for shareholder or board meetings generally do not need a full work permit, though ongoing operational management inside Türkiye requires proper work authorization—confirm your exact scope with a Turkish immigration attorney.

faq.q: Are foreign remote workers employed by an overseas company allowed to work on a tourist İkamet?
faq.a: Turkish labor rules prohibit unauthorized local employment, and tourist residence permits are not designed as work visas. Foreign remote workers should review Türkiye's dedicated Digital Nomad Visa or consult a licensed Turkish immigration lawyer.

faq.q: When must an employer register a foreign worker with SGK after permit approval?
faq.a: Employers must complete SGK social security registration and begin paying monthly premiums within statutory deadlines (typically within 30 days of permit start or entry into Türkiye) to keep the permit valid.

faq.q: How long is an initial Turkish work permit valid?
faq.a: A first-time work permit is generally issued for up to one year tied to a specific employer and workplace, followed by extensions of up to two years and then three years with the same employer.
